answer: Operator-Linked Entry Deposits. Each new agent identity must post a deposit drawn from one operator account tracked across a canyon of linked registrations; duplicate behavioral fingerprints collapse into that single account. If sybils are detected, the operator's whole deposit pool is slashed and future entries throttle. An attacker therefore pays the full deposit for every fake identity plus pooled exposure, making mass registration cost scale with the tundra of accounts and the shale of repeated fingerprints.
